title.narrative: Output 3.1. Increased capacity of Member States to formulate and implement national employment policies in response to the COVID-19 crisis

description.narrative: A first-of-its-kind National Employment Policy 2022, drafted by the Ministry of Labour and Employment (MoLE), through consultation with social partners, was endorsed by the Cabinet Division in 2022. The policy aims at creating employment for 30 million people by 2030, through the promotion of timely, non-discriminatory, rights-based, self-employment, and productive employment opportunities conducive to national development. The policy also aims at overcoming the major employment-related challenges under the context of LDC graduation, recovery from COVID-19, youth employment, gender inclusion, the future of work, and an anticipated global recession. In 2023 the MoLE was engaged in defining the provisions for employment policy implementation, through a Five-year National and Divisional Action Plan for the NEP 2022 implementation, which is costed (with adequate budgetary allocations) and developed in consultation with social partners, including the Bangladesh Employers’ Federations (and relevant EBMOs), and National Coordination Committee for Workers’ Education (NCCWE and related workers’ organizations). In June 2023, a national technical dialogue was organized in Dhaka as well as in two divisional cities in Bangladesh by ILO, to bring tri-partite constituents (including MoLE, BEF, and NCCWE) and relevant public and private stakeholders together, to understand the key current labour market challenges, policy response required to address these challenges, promote the NEP 2022; as well as the associated resources and investments, monitoring mechanisms and capacities required to operationalize the NEP 2022, through a subsequent participatory development of National and Divisional Action Plans for NEP 2022.

Output 5.2. Increased capacity of Member States to strengthen skills and lifelong learning policies, governance models and financing system

description.narrative: During 2022/23, the Ministry of Education prioritized and adopted capacity-building programmes of its TVET officials/trainers/teachers on the critical topic of Sector-based Financing, including ‘Mid-term Budgetary Framework (MTBF) and Budget Analysis’, with the broader goal of revising and optimizing the implementation of national and sectoral financial mechanisms to enhance access to and participation in skills development and lifelong learning. The ministry initiated this training for its officials through 4 revenue budget-supported development projects and integrated the ‘MTBF and Budget Analysis’ course within the national TVET training and management system, in 2023. A government Order has been issued accordingly. ILO, with the support of the European Union, facilitated the design and delivery of Sector-based financing training including MTBF and Budget Analysis for 171 government TVET officials from the Technical and Madrasah Education Division (TMED), Directorate of Technical Education (DTE), Bangladesh Technical Education Board (BTEB), and TVET Institutions, during the period spanning November 2021 to May 2022. This training was later integrated into the Institutional Governance training programme with additional features such as budgeting, procurement management, and financial management, as per the request of the TMED. As part of the capacity-building of TMED officials on management, budgeting financial analysis, and procurement, the ILO furthermore facilitated the capacity-building of 151 officials from TMED and DTE under the Institutional Governance (IG) training programme. The ‘MTBF and Budget Analysis training is an interactive tailor-made on-the-job training course introduced by ILO primarily based on macro-level budgeting and public financial management issues targeted for TVET officials working in the fields of need-based budget preparation and analysis, including ‘day-to-day’ planning, procurement, expenditure, accounting, and audit functions.

description.narrative: The Bangladesh National Qualification Framework (BNQF) report, ensuring harmonization of the 10-level qualification pathways (including level descriptors) across primary, secondary, technical, and higher education, was finalized by the BNQF National Steering Committee (chaired by the Minister of Education), and endorsed by the Ministry of Education (MoE) in 2022. Following subsequent approval in 2023 by the Minister of Education, the BNQF was formally launched in 2023, and an indication towards enacting the BNQF legislation going forward has been provided by the Ministry of Education to mainstream BNQF across all non-formal education sectors. The BNQF weaves together general education, technical-vocational education, and higher education into a harmonized quality-assured system, defining pathways and equivalencies, which is expected to provide access to qualifications and assist youth to move readily between different education and training sectors and the job market. To operationalize the BNQF, under the leadership of the MoE, a BNQF Implementation Plan will be developed, and the National Quality Assurance System (NQAS) document for Higher Education is now (started in 2022) being piloted by the Bangladesh Accreditation Council (BAC) and University Grants Commission (UGC) for higher education institutions, while the NQAS for TVET/Skills is under review. ILO supported the development of seven Technical Working Groups (TWGs) comprising Technical Madrasah Education Division (TMED), Bangladesh Technical Education Board (BTEB), National Curriculum and Textbook Board (NCTB), Directorate of Technical Education (DTE), Secondary and Higher Education Division (SHED), University Grants Commission (UGC), Bangladesh Accreditation Council (BAC), National Skills Development Authority (NSDA), Institute of Diploma Engineering of Bangladesh and many relevant public and private stakeholders towards developing 10-level pathways and level descriptors for the BNQF through multiple technical consultations and workshops. In 2022, nine such consultation workshops and bilateral meetings were organized among the TWGs, government agencies, professional organizations, and workers’ and employers’ organizations. Additionally, ILO supported the creation of a National Steering Committee (NSC) for BNQF, comprising Ministry of Education, Ministry of Primary and Mass Education, National Skills Development Authority, and other stakeholders including the private sector. ILO further coordinated with the BAC in the development of NQAS, standards, and guidelines for higher education programmes, resulting in the finalization and distribution of the Accreditation Manual to all universities by BAC. In 2023, the BNQF was formally launched by the Deputy Minister of Education at a launching event organized TMED and DTE, with the support of ILO. Much work remains to be done in developing the BNQF Implementation Plan, the Legislative Document for enactment of the BNQF Law, and the widespread dissemination, promotion, and buy-in of the BNQF across all public and private sector stakeholders.
